phases.name: Speak Chronicl3r contract v2

steps.name: Key-call results from the Chronicl3r client
criteria: Linking, looking up and deleting a key each return a KeyCallResult carrying the HTTP status, the contract code, any Retry-After seconds and the profile body on success

Every contract error code (missing_key, invalid_key, no_profiles, no_name_match, no_match, insufficient_data, ambiguous, upstream_rate_limited, upstream_unavailable, throttled, not_linked) is read from the JSON body
A non-JSON 404 reads as not_deployed; a timeout or connection failure reads as transport with no status; a DRF error without a code keeps only its status
No key call raises for an error status, and the link waits up to 60 s while lookup and delete wait up to 10 s
Neither a KeyCallResult nor its repr ever contains the submitted key or the profile's tacticus_user_id
The removed PATCH method and the duplicate profile getter no longer exist on the client
steps.implementation_notes: Approved plan item 1. Add a frozen dataclass KeyCallResult(status: int | None, code: str | None, retry_after: int | None, profile: dict | None) and three methods: link_api_key(key) -> POST player-profiles/api-keys/ (timeout 60), lookup_api_key(key) -> POST player-profiles/lookup/ (timeout 10), delete_api_key(tacticus_user_id) -> DELETE player-profiles/<id>/api-key/ (timeout 10). Body for the two POSTs is {'tacticus_player_api_key': key}. Route all three through ONE shared private helper that: never calls raise_for_status; catches requests.RequestException (covers Timeout and ConnectionError) and returns code='transport', status=None; parses the body as JSON and reads 'code' (absent -> None); treats a body that is not JSON (Content-Type not JSON, or .json() raising ValueError / requests.JSONDecodeError) on a 404 as code='not_deployed'; reads Retry-After as integer seconds (an HTTP-date or garbage -> None, the scheduler applies its own default); sets profile only on a 200. 204 has no body: status 204, code None, profile None. Declare `profile` with field(repr=False) so a logged result can never print the tacticus_user_id; the class holds no field for the key at all. The helper must not format the request body into any message. phases.name: Backfill the keys already held
phases.description: A pure scheduler decides which registrations are due and when the whole loop must back off; a two-minute loop in RegistrationCog uses cheap lookups to skip linked keys and spends at most one link per tick.

steps.name: Key-sync schedule
criteria: A registration the schedule has never seen is due at once; one whose key is linked is never due again while its key is unchanged
no_match is retried every 15 minutes and parked after 4 tries; no_name_match is retried 24 hours later
insufficient_data, ambiguous, invalid_key and missing_key park the player until the key changes; a changed key starts that player afresh
no_profiles and not_deployed pause the whole loop for an hour
upstream_rate_limited, upstream_unavailable, throttled and transport pause the whole loop for Retry-After, 300 s when absent, backing off on repeats
The schedule never holds a plaintext key
steps.implementation_notes: Approved plan item 3. New module bot/services/chronicl3r/key_sync.py: PURE, no I/O, no clock reads (the caller passes `now`), no logging. It must not import client.py (which runs load_dotenv() at import) or anything that reaches httpx (transitive archrule); stdlib only (hashlib, dataclasses, datetime). Its input vocabulary is plain values: (server_id, discord_id, key) triples for the current registrations, and recorded outcomes expressed as the contract code strings plus a 'linked' outcome (lookup 200 with has_valid_api_key true, or link 200) and a 'not_linked' outcome (lookup said the key is not held, so a link is due). State is keyed by (server_id, discord_id) and stores the SHA-256 hex fingerprint of the key, never the key; a fingerprint mismatch resets that player's state. The caller asks for due entries (distinguishing 'needs a lookup' from 'needs a link') and for whether the loop is paused; the key travels back to the caller only from the triples it passed in. Retry table exactly as the plan: linked -> done; no_match -> 15 min, max 4 tries then parked; no_name_match -> 24 h (no cap: the plan sets none); insufficient_data / ambiguous / invalid_key / missing_key -> parked until key change (or restart, since state is in-memory); no_profiles / not_deployed -> loop paused 1 h; upstream_rate_limited / upstream_unavailable / throttled / transport -> loop paused for retry_after or 300 s. REFINEMENTS the plan left open, pinned here so the crafter does not invent them: (a) backoff = consecutive transient pauses double the wait from max(retry_after, 300) s, capped at 3600 s, reset by any non-pause outcome; (b) any outcome not in the table (a code-less 401/403/5xx, a non-JSON non-404) is treated as a transient pause with the default — it protects the 60/h budget and a configuration error then surfaces in the logs at most hourly. Tests: Hypothesis over sequences of (registration sets, outcomes, clock advances); a RuleBasedStateMachine is welcome for the interleavings. The plaintext property walks the scheduler's state recursively (vars, containers, repr, pickle bytes) and asserts no generated key string appears. steps.name: Background key-sync loop in RegistrationCog
criteria: Each tick looks up at most 20 due keys across every server, marks already-linked ones done without spending a link, and posts at most one link
While the schedule says the loop is paused, a tick makes no Chronicl3r call
Setting CHRONICL3R_KEY_SYNC=off stops every Chronicl3r call from the loop
A tick that fails for any reason is logged and the loop keeps running
The loop starts with the cog, waits for the bot to be ready, and stops when the cog unloads
A link made by /registration register is recorded, so the loop does not repeat it
No sync log line carries a key or a tacticus_user_id
steps.implementation_notes: Approved plan item 4 (loop half). RegistrationCog.__init__ builds the scheduler from 03-01 and starts `chronicler_key_sync`, a @tasks.loop(minutes=2); cog_unload cancels it; its before_loop awaits bot.wait_until_ready (pattern: tasks_cog.py TasksCog.__init__ / cog_unload). Tick: read CHRONICL3R_KEY_SYNC each tick (case-insensitive 'off' -> return before any call); if the scheduler is paused, return; gather (server_id, discord_id, key) for every entry with a key across repo.list_server_ids() + load_player_registrations(server_id); ask the scheduler for due entries; run up to 20 `player_service.lookup_key` calls on entries needing a lookup, recording each outcome; then at most ONE `player_service.link_key` on an entry needing a link, recording its outcome; stop the tick at the first outcome that pauses the loop. Whole tick body in try/except Exception, logged (suggested event 'chronicler.key_sync.tick_failed'), so the loop never dies. Budget: one link per 2 min = 30/h, leaving half of Chronicl3r's 60/h per-account throttle for live registrations. Lookups have their own 6000/h bucket. Also in this step: `register` records its own link outcome in the same scheduler so a key just linked or just refused is not immediately re-posted by the loop.
